questions.q: What is the keeper's rule in Kessel?
questions.a: The lamp turns when the clock strikes the hour, and a keeper who breaks it loses the tower.

questions.q: How does Ines pay Ada, and why?
questions.a: With her mother's brass compass, because she cannot pay Ada's price.

questions.q: What will Ines's father lose if the clock is not running by Friday?
questions.a: The tower and the house that goes with it.

screens.label: In short
screens.text: Ines, the keeper's daughter, finds the lighthouse clock stopped. Mr Hale, the harbour master, warns that her father will lose the tower, so she pays Ada, a clockmaker, with her mother's compass.

takeaway.label: Why it matters
takeaway.text: Under the keeper's rule, the lamp turns on the clock's hour, or the keeper loses the tower.

scenes.text: {On the first cold morning} Ines finds the clock in [the lighthouse] stopped, so the lamp does not turn; Tomas, her brother, says nothing.
At [the harbour], Mr Hale warns that the keeper will lose the tower unless the clock runs by Friday.
{That evening} Ada agrees on [the quay] to mend the clock, because Ines offers her mother's compass.
{That night} Ines gives Ada the key at [the house], and the clockmaker climbs the tower.

items.title: Ines
items.text: The keeper's daughter; she holds the key to the clock room while her father is away.

items.title: Tomas
items.text: Ines's younger brother; he says nothing when she says somebody stopped the clock.

items.title: Mr Hale
items.text: The harbour master; he says the clock is the family's problem, not his.

items.title: Ada
items.text: A clockmaker from the city, come to repair the church clock.

screens.label: What happens in full
paragraphs: The lighthouse clock at Kessel stops before dawn, so the lamp does not turn. Under the keeper's rule, the lamp turns when the clock strikes the hour, and a keeper who breaks the rule loses the tower. Ines, whose father is away, climbs to the clock room; Tomas, her younger brother, says nothing when she says somebody stopped it.

At the harbour, three boats wait for the light. Mr Hale, the harbour master, warns that the keeper will lose the tower and the house unless the clock runs by Friday, and he will not help. Ada, a clockmaker, arrives on the late evening boat; Ines cannot pay her price, so she gives her mother's brass compass. That night Ines gives Ada the key, and Ada climbs the tower.

rows.name: The keeper's rule
rows.text: The lamp turns when the clock strikes the hour; a keeper who breaks it loses the tower.

items.title: When and where
items.text: The night the clock stopped; Ines is at the house, and Ada is at the top of the tower.

items.title: Who is there
items.text: Ines, the keeper's daughter, and Ada, the clockmaker, who now holds the key to the clock room.

items.title: What they want
items.text: Ines wants the clock running by Friday, so her father keeps the tower.

items.title: What just happened
items.text: Ines could not pay Ada's price, so she gave her mother's compass and the key.

rows.name: Tomas's silence
rows.text: Why does Tomas say nothing about the clock?

questions.q: Why did the lighthouse clock stop?
questions.a: Somebody packed salt into the teeth of its main wheel, after opening the case with a key.

questions.q: Who borrowed the key from Tomas?
questions.a: Mr Hale, the harbour master, for one evening, for a silver coin.

questions.q: From Chapter 1: What will Ines's father lose if the clock is not running by Friday?
questions.a: The tower and the house that goes with it.

screens.label: In short
screens.text: Ada finds salt packed into the clock's main wheel, so somebody used a key. Tomas admits he lent the key to Mr Hale; Ines will not give it to him again.

takeaway.label: Why it matters
takeaway.text: Only two keys open the clock room, and Mr Hale borrowed one.

scenes.text: {At dawn} Ada shows Ines salt from the main wheel in [the kitchen], so Tomas admits he lent Mr Hale the key.
{At noon} the mended clock strikes in [the lighthouse], so the lamp turns and the boats come in.
{In the afternoon} Mr Hale thanks Ada and asks for the key, but Ines says her father will decide.
{When he has gone} Ines hides the key in the base of the lamp in [the kitchen].

items.title: Tomas
items.text: Ines's younger brother; he lent the key to Mr Hale for one evening, for a silver coin.

items.title: Mr Hale
items.text: The harbour master; he borrowed the key and now asks Ines for it.

items.title: Ada
items.text: The clockmaker; she found the salt, keeps it, and stays in Kessel to mend the church clock.

screens.label: What happens in full
paragraphs: Ada works through the night and finds salt packed into the main wheel: salt does not stop a clock by chance, so somebody opened the case with a key. Only two keys exist, and Tomas admits he lent his sister's to Mr Hale for one evening, for a silver coin.

Ada mends the clock; at noon it strikes, the lamp turns and the boats come in. Mr Hale asks Ines for the key, and she says her father will decide on Friday. She hides the key in the base of the kitchen lamp. Ada will stay in Kessel and keeps the salt.

items.title: When and where
items.text: The evening after the clock runs again; Ines sits by the window until dark.

items.title: Who is there
items.text: Ines, the keeper's daughter, alone, with the key hidden in the kitchen lamp.

items.title: What they want
items.text: Ines wants her father to keep the tower; Mr Hale wants the key kept at the harbour office.

items.title: What just happened
items.text: Mr Hale asked for the key, so Ines said her father would decide, and hid it.
